name: Vespid Dynamics Insect-Scale Manufacturing
description: A manufacturing methodology for producing electronic and mechanical components at the scale of insects — circuits, sensors, actuators, and structural elements measured in millimeters. ISM uses micro-lithography, precision robotic assembly, and self-organizing nanomaterial deposition to build functional devices small enough to be embedded in a grain of rice. The technology underlies Vespid's micro-drone platforms, but its applications extend to medical implants, surveillance devices, and electronic warfare payloads that are too small to detect with conventional inspection.
social_impact: ISM has made surveillance and control technologies that are physically invisible to unaided human inspection. A complete functional sensor package smaller than a grain of sand can be embedded in any material, surface, or object — and in a person, through their food, their clothing, or their medical care — without any chance of visual detection. The technology has created a justified paranoia about the invisible: anything could contain a sensor, and the only defense is knowing it is there.
story_hooks: ISM-fabricated surveillance devices have been found embedded in the paper of printed documents — every physical document passing through a specific printer has been bugged at the paper level.

An ISM manufacturing facility has experienced a contamination event where micro-scale devices escaped containment and are now embedded in the facility's building materials — the walls are literally watching.
